security_audit.summary: This is a Chinese-language educational guide for Claude Code, consisting entirely of Markdown documentation (SKILL.md plus references/README.md and references/index.md). All 235 static findings are pattern matches inside tutorial code fences and prose — illustrative bash, JavaScript, and configuration examples that teach Claude Code usage — and none represent executable behavior shipped by the skill. I marked 234 findings as false positives (shell substitutions, ~/.claude config paths, ../add-dir examples, a sudo example, hex-encoding, and high-entropy heuristics all being documentation, not runnable code). The single confirmed finding is low-confidence and non-security: SKILL.md's YAML frontmatter is malformed (a leading 'TRANSLATED CONTENT:' line before the opening '---'), which blocked static scanning; manual review confirms that file is benign. No data exfiltration, obfuscation, prompt injection, or credential harvesting was found.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md has malformed YAML frontmatter: a 'TRANSLATED CONTENT:' line appears before the opening '---' delimiter, so the frontmatter block is not at the top of the file and could not be parsed or statically scanned.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the leading 'TRANSLATED CONTENT:' line (and any content before it) so the file begins with the '---' frontmatter delimiter on line 1. This restores parseable name/description metadata and lets the file be scanned normally.

remediation.issue: The guide contains many example shell and JavaScript snippets that reference ~/.claude paths, sudo, and $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. These are safe as documentation but could be copy-pasted by readers without understanding their effect.
remediation.suggestion: Where practical, add brief cautionary notes near sensitive examples (e.g., the sudo restart and API-key echo snippets) reminding readers to review commands before running them and to avoid printing secrets in shared terminals.

content.user_title: Master Advanced Claude Code Development in Chinese
content.value_statement: Learning Claude Code's advanced features from scattered English sources is slow for Chinese-speaking developers. This guide gathers the core tools, workflows, MCP integration, and best practices into one structured Chinese reference.
actual_capabilities: Explains the seven core Claude Code tools: REPL, Artifacts, Web Search, Web Fetch, Conversation Search, Recent Chats, and End Conversation.
Describes a staged workflow for analyzing large files using line, word, and structure inspection before reading targeted sections.
Documents MCP server configuration through the mcp_config.json file and how Claude discovers MCP tools.
Covers the hooks system configured in settings.json, including pre-use, post-use, and prompt-submit events.
Presents advanced patterns such as multi-agent delegation, task management with TodoWrite, and validation-driven development.
Provides troubleshooting guidance for tool permission errors, REPL performance, and MCP connection failures.
limitations: The content is written entirely in Chinese, so it is best suited to Chinese-speaking readers.
It is reference documentation only; it contains no executable scripts and performs no actions.
Some described features are experimental or reflect observed patterns rather than official guarantees, so details may change.
Code snippets are illustrative examples and should be reviewed before being adapted to real projects.

use_cases.title: Onboard a Chinese-speaking developer to Claude Code
use_cases.description: A developer new to Claude Code reads the guide to understand the core tools, permission model, and typical workflows before starting real work.
use_cases.target_user: Developers who prefer Chinese-language learning material

use_cases.title: Set up MCP and hooks for a team
use_cases.description: A team lead uses the MCP and hooks sections to configure server connections and automation such as formatting and test-running for a shared project.
use_cases.target_user: Team leads configuring Claude Code environments

use_cases.title: Reference advanced workflow patterns during a task
use_cases.description: An experienced user consults the advanced-patterns and troubleshooting sections when handling large files, multi-agent tasks, or connection errors.
use_cases.target_user: Experienced Claude Code users seeking quick reference

prompt_templates.title: Explain a core tool
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this guide, explain what the Claude Code REPL tool does and give one simple example of reading a file with it.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a large-file analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Based on the large-file analysis workflow in this guide, outline the steps I should follow to review a 9000-line Markdown document.

prompt_templates.title: Configure an MCP server
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me, using the guide's MCP section, how to add a new MCP server entry to my configuration and explain each field.

prompt_templates.title: Design a multi-agent workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Using the advanced patterns in this guide, help me design a multi-agent workflow where one agent reviews code while another writes tests, and describe how results return to the main agent.

output_examples.input: Explain the difference between tools that are auto-granted and tools that need authorization.
output_examples.output: Auto-granted tools include the REPL, Artifacts, Web Search, Web Fetch, and Conversation Search, which run in restricted sandboxes. Tools that need explicit authorization include Bash, Edit, and Write, because they can read or modify the filesystem. The guide recommends granting only the minimum permissions a task requires.

output_examples.input: What are the recommended stages for analyzing a large file?
output_examples.output: The guide recommends three stages. First, quantitative assessment using line, word, and character counts. Second, structure analysis by extracting headings and locating code blocks. Third, targeted content extraction by reading specific sections rather than the whole file at once.

best_practices: Grant tools only the permissions a task truly needs, following the least-privilege guidance in the guide.
Analyze large files in stages, inspecting structure and counts before reading full content.
Review any example command or snippet from the guide before running it in a real environment.
anti_patterns: Copying example shell commands such as sudo restarts directly into production without reviewing their effect.
Treating the illustrative code snippets as ready-to-ship scripts rather than teaching examples.
Storing secrets or API keys in configuration or hooks shown in examples without securing them properly.

faq.question: What is this skill?
faq.answer: It is a comprehensive Chinese-language guide to advanced Claude Code development, covering tools, workflows, MCP integration, hooks, and best practices.

faq.question: Does this skill run any code or scripts?
faq.answer: No. It is reference documentation only. All code shown is illustrative and is not executed by the skill.

faq.question: What language is the content written in?
faq.answer: The main content is written in Chinese, with some English terms and code examples.

faq.question: Who is this guide best suited for?
faq.answer: It is best suited for Chinese-speaking developers who want to learn or reference advanced Claude Code features and workflows.

faq.question: Does it cover MCP and hooks?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes sections on configuring MCP servers and on setting up hooks for automation such as formatting and testing.

faq.question: Are the code examples safe to use directly?
faq.answer: The examples are teaching material. Review and adapt them to your own environment, and be careful with commands that change system state or handle secrets.
